items.name: DO_ONCE_LITE Print-Exactly-Once Sentinel (warnOnce)
items.counter_case: A static Set that only grows means old once-flags are never collected; in a long-lived Cortex process this is a trivial leak (one string per unique warning site), which is acceptable.

items.name: Ratelimit State — Burst + Interval + Missed Counter
items.counter_case: Cortex is single-threaded Node.js so the atomic ops are unnecessary; a plain counter + Date.now() comparison suffices and avoids porting the spinlock semantics.

items.name: WMARK Three-Level Graduated Cache Pressure
items.counter_case: Three thresholds add three config knobs; Cortex's surface-don't-act principle means users rarely tune these, so the added complexity may not be justified over a simpler high/low pair.

items.name: Missed-Counter Drain on Exit — Suppression Summary
items.counter_case: Cortex sessions often die via Ctrl-C without clean shutdown; a drain in process.on('exit') is unreliable for async log writes and may be silently skipped.

items.name: RCU Generation-Pointer Snapshot Reads
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded; there is no true concurrent reader-writer race. The generation-pointer discipline still has value for correctness during async operations but is not strictly necessary.

items.name: percpu_counter Batched Approximate Token Counting
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded and has no per-CPU shards; the only benefit is reducing how often the central counter is written, which matters only if Cortex is doing thousands of increments per second.

items.name: kfifo Power-of-2 Mask Lockless Ring Queue
items.symbol: struct __kfifo { in, out, mask, esize, data }, INIT_KFIFO, kfifo_len = in - out, kfifo_is_full
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded so the lockless SPSC property is irrelevant; plain arrays with length checks are simpler and V8 handles them efficiently at Cortex's scale.

items.name: Timer Wheel Multi-Level Bucket
items.symbol: LVL_CLK_SHIFT=3, LVL_SIZE=64, LVL_DEPTH=9, WHEEL_SIZE=576, calc_index(), calc_wheel_index()
items.violated_principle: Node.js setTimeout already uses a native timer wheel at the libuv layer; building a second wheel in JS adds complexity for a performance gain invisible at Cortex's scale (<100 concurrent timers)

items.name: RCU Segmented Callback List — Age-Segmented Deferred Work Queue
items.symbol: RCU_DONE_TAIL, RCU_WAIT_TAIL, RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL, RCU_NEXT_TAIL, struct rcu_segcblist
items.violated_principle: Node.js fs.createWriteStream with backpressure already provides a two-state model that covers 90% of this benefit; the four-segment model adds significant conceptual overhead for marginal gain at Cortex's write volume
